# Verify the Nahuatl translation of "I fall" using the given data.

data = {
    5: ("titzāhtzi", "you shout"),
    9: ("kochi in tīzītl", "the healer sleeps"),
    17: ("tēhuetzītia in zihuātl", "the woman makes somebody fall"),
    14: ("tiktēkāhualtia in oktli", "you make somebody leave the wine"),
}

submitted = "nitēhuetzā"

# Step 1: derive the base intransitive stem from the causative in sentence 17.
caus = data[17][0].split()[0]            # tēhuetzītia
assert caus.startswith("tē")
body = caus[len("tē"):]                  # huetzītia
assert body.endswith("ītia")
stem = body[:-len("ītia")] + "i"         # huetz + i -> huetzi (causative -ītia replaces final -i)
print("causative:", caus, "-> base intransitive stem:", stem)

# Step 2: confirm that intransitive present verbs take subject prefix + bare stem
# (e.g., ti-tzāhtzi "you shout", kochi "sleeps") and end in -i, with no tē- object marker.
shout = data[5][0]
assert shout == "ti" + "tzāhtzi"
print("pattern check: ti + tzāhtzi =", shout, "(prefix + bare stem ending in -i)")

# Step 3: tē- marks an indefinite human object (sentences 14, 17); intransitive "fall" has no object.
print("tē- appears in object-marked causatives:", data[14][0].split()[0], caus)

# Step 4: build the expected form for 1st person singular.
expected = "ni" + stem
print("expected:", expected)
print("submitted:", submitted)

# Step 5: compare the submission.
issues = []
if "tē" in submitted:
    issues.append("contains object prefix tē- (somebody), which is not in 'I fall'")
if not submitted.endswith("i"):
    issues.append("ending is not the bare stem ending -i seen in the intransitive pattern")
print("issues:", issues)

if submitted == expected:
    print("CHECK PASS")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL")
